_header: Extra header fields after the four fixed integers (magic, version, format digest, kernel schema, compiler identity), in declaration order. `string` is length-prefixed UTF-8. `app_id` is the app identity, reverse-DNS (LLP 1023 D5): bake writes it from DataSource::app_id(); empty is unnamed (a fixture or a stand-in) and unnamed matches anything at boot. LLP 1038 D2: router names the root slot filled before initializers.

header.name: locale
header._comment: @ref LLP 1060 D4: the root string slot holding the resolved locale every `t(...)` reads; set only when the app calls `t`. The runner writes it from set_place.

_about: The single declaration authority for the plan: its tables, the expression VM's opcodes, the stdlib roster, and the enum vocabularies. plan/build.rs generates the row structs, the canonical encoder, the validating decoder, the opcode and stdlib enums, and FORMAT_DIGEST from this file. Nothing here is hand-mirrored anywhere else. Kernel node types, props, and style rows are NOT declared here: plan rows carry the kernel's ordinals as numbers, and the crates that give them meaning take the vocabulary from exact-kernel (LLP 1004 D2).
_codecs: u8 | u16 | u32 | i32 | f64 | bool | str (u32 index into the string pool) | enum:<Name> (u8 ordinal) | idx:<table> (u32 row index, validated) | opt:<table> (u32 row index or NONE = 0xFFFFFFFF) | range:<table> (u32 start + u32 len, validated) | code (u32 offset + u32 len into the code pool, validated as well-formed bytecode) | bytes (u32 offset + u32 len into the data pool)
_tables: Document order is significant: nodes and regions with the same parent are ordered by `order`; an arm's content is every node and region whose `arm` names it; a node with no parent inside an arm is one of the arm's roots. Fonts are static in v1: a face is exactly one source path, weight, and italic flag. Variable-axis ranges are additive later, never inferred from the file by a host.

fields.name: placeholder
fields._comment: @ref LLP 1048.003 D6: the row whose value shows while this one's source hasn't answered and nothing is kept for its arguments — a declared `else source(args)`, compiled as a row of its own (named `<name>#else`, arguments that read no state, the same type, no placeholder of its own). None: a list or an option shows its empty value, and anything else has none.

fields.name: placeholder_value
fields._comment: @ref LLP 1054.000.002 D3: a declared `else empty(field=value, …)`, the compiler's constant (a value), shown while nothing is kept and the source has not answered. Empty bytes: none — an undeclared placeholder is the type's zero, which the runner computes (D1).

fields.name: refreshes
fields._comment: @ref LLP 1054.000.000 D1: the resources a send to this mutation refreshes, forced, when it runs and when its reply lands (`mutation m as shape T refreshes a, b`).

fields.name: then
fields._comment: The action a `mutation … then action` runs after each answer lands, as its own commit (LLP 1016.001). None: nothing runs.

fields.name: render
fields._comment: @ref LLP 1048 D2, LLP 1048.003 D5: when the route's document renders; undeclared is client.

fields.name: activate
fields._comment: @ref LLP 1048.003 D5: when a rendered page's runtime loads; inferred when undeclared.

fields.name: pages
fields._comment: @ref LLP 1048.000 D2, LLP 1048.003 D5: the source that lists a parameterized route's pages — the values of its one parameter, a list<string> — for the build to render and the server's sitemap to name. Empty: none.

fields.name: pages_args
fields._comment: @ref LLP 1048.000 D2: that source's arguments, values (a list in the plan's value encoding); empty bytes without a source.

tables.name: keyframes
tables._comment: @ref LLP 1055 D5: the app's `@keyframes` rules by name, each body as CSS text (`0%{r:3px;}100%{r:9px;}`); the runner resolves `animation-name` against them.

tables.name: texts
tables._comment: @ref LLP 1060 D3: one localized text, `{name}` placeholders unfilled. Within a locale, sorted by key.

tables.name: locales
tables._comment: @ref LLP 1060 D3: one strings table per locale (BCP 47 name). Row 0 is the base; the rest are in name order. rtl is the CLDR script direction, compiled once. Table names remain for data-only strings. Only the keys the app's `t` calls name.

_enums: Wire ordinal is the 0-based index. An unknown ordinal is a typed decode rejection.
_opcodes: The expression VM: a stack machine over values with a small locals stack (`BindLocal` pops into it, `LoadLocal` copies from it, `DropLocal` pops it) for names an inline `match` binds and the item and index a `Map`/`Filter` callback binds. Each opcode names its operand layout; the decoder validates framing and every index operand. `depth` operands count enclosing instance scopes (0 = innermost). Type inference guarantees stack discipline; the VM still traps, never UB.

opcodes.name: LoadIndex
opcodes._comment: LLP 1062 D8: the position (a number from 0) of the `each` row `depth` scopes out, as `each item, i in list` names it.

opcodes.name: Map
opcodes._comment: @ref LLP 1017.003 D5: pops a list; runs the callback body that follows inline up to the operand's offset once per item, with the item and its index bound as the next two locals; pushes the list of the values the body leaves.

opcodes.name: Filter
opcodes._comment: @ref LLP 1017.003 D5: as `Map`, keeping each item whose body leaves `true`.

_stdlib: The enumerated roster (LLP 1004 D2/D4): every callable an expression may name, with its parameter types and return type (`any` = one of number, string, bool, list). The compiler checks calls against this table; the runner's VM implements each entry once; entries are added by fixture, never by speculation. LLP 1038 D3: Router and Entry name reserved record shapes; list<Router>, list<Entry>, and list<string> are typed lists.

stdlib.name: trim
stdlib._comment: @ref LLP 1054.000.005 D1: JavaScript's String.prototype.trim — ECMA-262 WhiteSpace and LineTerminator, not Rust's White_Space.

stdlib.name: first
stdlib._comment: @ref LLP 1054.000 C4: a list's first item, `some(x)`, or `none` for an empty list; `any` is `list<T>` in and `option<T>` out (the type checker's).

stdlib.name: t
stdlib._comment: @ref LLP 1060 D2: the text for (locale, key), placeholders filled from name/value pairs. The compiler writes every argument; an author writes `t("key", name=value)`.

stdlib.name: map
stdlib._comment: @ref LLP 1017.003 D4: `map(list<T>, (T, number) => U) -> list<U>` (the type checker's). Lowered to the `Map` opcode, never `Call`: the row reserves the name.

stdlib.name: filter
stdlib._comment: @ref LLP 1017.003 D4: `filter(list<T>, (T, number) => bool) -> list<T>`. Lowered to the `Filter` opcode, never `Call`.

stdlib.name: join
stdlib._comment: @ref LLP 1017.003 D4: the web's `Array.prototype.join` over a list of strings, numbers or bools, each printed as `toString` prints it.

_sources: LLP 1027 D2: the data seam's signatures. One row per data-source name the app's `resource` and `send` declarations use, with the parameter types and the result type every use agrees on (the compiler refuses a disagreement by name). An executor that marshals by shape — the TypeScript module's — reads this table at bind; a Rust crate ignores it. formatVersion 3.
_resources: `reader` (formatVersion 4, LLP 1027 D4 as ruled 2026-09-03): the bake found this resource consulting the store. Its `initial` is then the empty-store answer — the fresh install's first frame, never a developer's session (the bake's store is empty by construction, LLP 1018 D4) — and the runner treats it as a placeholder: a kept answer from the device's store beats it, and a data source that is not ready at boot (a TypeScript module before its host loads it) is asked again at `data_ready`. LLP 1038 D5: initial_args is a canonical Value::List of evaluated bake arguments, empty bytes only without a compiled value; initial is reused only for equal arguments.
